newsitem.title: UK: Pearson may make 100 mln pounds provision.
newsitem.headline: Pearson may make 100 mln pounds provision.

text.p: British media and leisure firm Pearson Plc said on Thursday that it has uncovered improper accounting at Penguin USA, its U.S. trade book publishing subsidiary, that may lead to a charge against 1996 profits of as much as 100 million pounds ($163.4 million).
It said in a statement that the problems date back to 1991 and relate to unauthorised discounts, given to customers in return for early payments.
Pearson said that these discounts were not correctly recognised within Penguin US accounts. It noted that they did not take place at any other Penguin companies outside the U.S.
"The profits of Penguin will not be restated and Pearson has not changed its 1997 profit expectations for the company," said Pearson in a statement.
The company said it has launched an independent investigation by outside counsel and by its recently appointed auditors, Price Waterhouse.
"We have moved quickly to implement a detailed plan of action to address these unauthorised practices," said Marjorie Scardino, chief executive of Pearson.

Pearson had 1995 pretax profits of 365.1 million pounds ($596.5 million), boosted by a capital gain of 131 million, on sales of 1.83 billion pounds. Penguin US gross sales, before allowances for books returned were in excess of 300 million pounds in 1996.
